newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics off, traders cite analyst comments.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics off, traders cite analyst comments.

text.p: Shares of U.S. Robotics fell five to 75-7/8 at midday Tuesday after an analyst cautioned the modem maker may be facing a weak quarter as it makes the transition to new technology, according to market sources.
Options traders and an analyst who asked not to be named said Needham & Co warned that U.S. Robotics' current fiscal first quarter may be weak. Needham & Co declined comment.
U.S. Robotics executives have met with analysts recently regarding earnings this quarter. The company was not immediately available for comment on the meetings.
"I heard that Needham made a negative comment this morning and apparently they were saying the quarter is going to be weak," the analyst said.
"There is a product transition issue, so the company has always been very cautious," he continued, adding that he met recently with U.S. Robotics executives.
"They think the quarter will be fine but it's too early to say how it's going to pan out," he said.

The product transition refers to U.S. Robotics' new "x2" technology, which allows Internet users to receive information at speeds of 56 kilobit per second over conventional telephone lines. The fastest modem on the market now has speed capabilities of 33.6 kbps.
The new technology will be available in early 1997, but U.S. Robotics has offered upgrades for modems purchased now.
